pencereler.0-5: Near Buffalo, a commuter plane suddenly stalled and fell onto a house. Everyone aboard
pencereler.5-12: was killed, along with one person on the ground. As the plane slowed, its stall warning shook the controls.
pencereler.12-20: The right response was to push the nose down. The captain pulled back instead. That deepened the stall until recovery was impossible.
pencereler.20-30: Both pilots had been tired. US rules on pilot training and rest were then overhauled.

bulgular: 12-20s: no central mystery or problem is posed

segmentler.metin: Colgan Air Flight 3407 stalled and crashed into a house near Buffalo.
It took only a pilot pulling back when the stall warning shook the controls.
So how could a pilot pulling back when the stall warning shook the controls do this?
The answer is inappropriate response to the stick shaker, deepening an aerodynamic stall — and it is why US pilot training, rest and experience rules were overhauled.
